# 1 Kings Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** As David's life neared its end, he gave Solomon his son these final instructions:

**2** "I am about to die, as all people must. Be strong. Show that you are a man.

**3** Carry out the duties the LORD your God has given you. Walk in his ways. Keep his laws, his commands, his rules, and his decrees, as they are written in the Law of Moses — so that you will succeed in everything you do, wherever you go.

**4** Then the LORD will keep the promise he made to me: 'If your descendants are faithful to me, walking before me wholeheartedly, you will always have a man on the throne of Israel.'

**5** Now, you know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me — how he murdered two commanders of Israel's armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them in peacetime as if in war, staining his belt and sandals with innocent blood.

**6** Use your own judgment, but do not let him die a peaceful death.

**7** Show kindness to the sons of Barzillai of Gilead. Let them eat at your table, because they stood by me when I was fleeing from your brother Absalom.

**8** And there is Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, who cursed me viciously the day I left for Mahanaim. When he came to meet me at the Jordan, I swore to him by the LORD that I would not kill him.

**9** But you must not let him go unpunished. You are a wise man — you will know what to do. Make sure his gray head goes down to the grave in blood."

**10** Then David died and was buried in the City of David.

**11** He had reigned over Israel for forty years — seven in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.

**12** Solomon took his seat on the throne of his father David, and his rule was firmly established.

**13** Adonijah son of Haggith went to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother. "Have you come in peace?" she asked. "Yes, in peace," he said.

**14** Then he said, "I need to ask you something." "Go ahead," she said.

**15** He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine — all Israel expected me to be king. But things changed, and the kingdom went to my brother. It was the LORD's doing.

**16** Now I have just one request. Please don't turn me down." "What is it?" she asked.

**17** "Please ask King Solomon — he won't refuse you — to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife."

**18** "Very well," Bathsheba said. "I'll speak to the king for you."

**19** When Bathsheba went to King Solomon on Adonijah's behalf, the king stood up to greet her and bowed to her. He sat down on his throne and had a chair brought for his mother, who sat at his right hand.

**20** "I have one small request," she said. "Please don't turn me down." The king replied, "Ask away, Mother. I won't refuse you."

**21** She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife."

**22** King Solomon exploded: "Why are you asking for Abishag for Adonijah? You might as well ask for the kingdom for him! He is my older brother, and he has Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah on his side!"

**23** Then Solomon swore by the LORD: "May God strike me dead if Adonijah does not pay for this with his life!

**24** As surely as the LORD lives — the God who established me on my father David's throne and gave me a dynasty as he promised — Adonijah will die today."

**25** King Solomon gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who went and struck Adonijah down. He died.

**26** To Abiathar the priest, the king said, "Go home to Anathoth. You deserve to die, but I won't kill you now because you carried the ark of the Lord GOD for my father David and shared in all his hardships."

**27** So Solomon removed Abiathar from the priesthood — fulfilling what the LORD had spoken long ago against the house of Eli at Shiloh.

**28** When Joab heard the news — for Joab had backed Adonijah, though he had not backed Absalom — he ran to the tent of the LORD and grabbed the horns of the altar.

**29** When Solomon was told that Joab had taken refuge at the altar, he sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada with orders: "Go and strike him down."

**30** Benaiah went to the tent of the LORD and said, "The king says, 'Come out.'" But Joab answered, "No. I will die here." Benaiah reported back to the king.

**31** The king said, "Do what he says — strike him down right there. Bury him, and clear from me and my father's house the guilt of the innocent blood Joab shed.

**32** The LORD will repay him for his bloodshed. He struck down two men who were better and more righteous than he was — Abner son of Ner, commander of Israel's army, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of Judah's army — and he murdered them without my father David's knowledge.

**33** May the guilt of their blood rest on Joab and his descendants forever. But may David and his descendants, his house and his throne, have the LORD's peace forever."

**34** So Benaiah son of Jehoiada went and struck Joab down and killed him. He was buried at his home in the wilderness.

**35** The king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada as army commander in Joab's place, and Zadok as priest in Abiathar's place.

**36** Then the king summoned Shimei and told him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not leave the city for any reason.

**37** The day you cross the Kidron Valley, you are a dead man. And it will be your own fault."

**38** Shimei agreed: "That is fair. I will do as my lord the king says." And Shimei lived in Jerusalem for a long time.

**39** But three years later, two of Shimei's slaves ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. When Shimei was told, "Your slaves are in Gath,"

**40** he saddled his donkey and went to Gath to get them back.

**41** When Solomon learned that Shimei had left Jerusalem and gone to Gath and come back,

**42** the king summoned him. "Didn't I make you swear by the LORD?" he said. "Didn't I warn you clearly: 'The day you leave this city, you will die'? And you said, 'Fair enough. I agree.'

**43** So why didn't you keep the oath you swore before the LORD? Why did you disobey my command?"

**44** The king continued, "You know in your heart every wicked thing you did to my father David. Now the LORD is bringing your wickedness down on your own head.

**45** But King Solomon will be blessed, and David's throne will stand secure before the LORD forever."

**46** Then the king gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He went out and struck Shimei down, and he died. And the kingdom was firmly in Solomon's hands.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **2:2 — "Show that you are a man"**: David's deathbed charge combines covenant theology (v. 3-4) with ruthless political housekeeping (v. 5-9). The "be a man" instruction turns out to mean: handle the killing I couldn't do while I was alive.

2. **2:22 — Solomon's eruption**: Bathsheba's innocent request triggers an explosion because Solomon understands what she apparently does not: asking for a king's concubine is tantamount to claiming the throne. Solomon sees through Adonijah's ploy instantly.

3. **2:26-27 — Abiathar's exile**: The only enemy Solomon spares — and only because of past loyalty to David and the ark. The narrator's editorial comment connects this to the Eli prophecy, drawing a line across centuries of narrative.

4. **2:30 — "I will die here"**: Joab's final stand is at the altar — the place of sanctuary. Solomon's willingness to violate altar sanctuary shows the ruthlessness of the new regime and the severity of Joab's crimes.

5. **2:46 — "the kingdom was firmly in Solomon's hands"**: This single sentence closes the succession narrative that began with David's sin with Bathsheba. Three deaths (Adonijah, Joab, Shimei) and one exile (Abiathar) — and the bloodiest transition of power in Israel's history is complete.

— PNEUMA
